hints: Read the string left to right. When a ) appears, either something is open for it or it is not. And what about the (s still open when you reach the end?
Balance counting (a stack that only stores a count). Keep open = number of unmatched (. A ) with open == 0 needs one inserted (; every ( still open at the end needs one inserted ).

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Push '(' onto a real stack and pop on matching ')', counting unmatched ')' and the leftover stack size.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Replace the stack with a single counter of open brackets.

explain: For "())(": ( makes open = 1; ) closes it, open = 0; the next ) has nothing to close, so insert = 1; the last ( makes open = 1. The answer is insert + open = 2. Each fix is forced: an unmatched ) must get a ( before it, and an unmatched ( must get a ) after it, so the count is minimal. An empty string correctly returns 0.
recognize: Only one bracket type and you only need counts, not positions → a balance counter instead of a full stack.
